title: AI is speeding up executive hiring, but some parts still take people
excerpt: C-suite recruiters say AI is accelerating research and widening talent pools. Judgment, consensus-building, and courtship remain distinctly human.
content_html:
AI is accelerating many parts of executive-level hiring, though other parts remain constrained by distinctly human obstacles.

Recruiters say homing in on suitable candidates can account for as much as half the work in high-stakes C-suite job searches. AI can speed up that process by mapping the market, surfacing names, combing through years of internal notes, and suggesting unconventional talent pools.

"The identification of candidates is going to become commoditized," said Marty Parker, CEO of Waterstone Human Capital, an executive search and culture advisory firm.

Meanwhile, other parts of the recruiting process remain slow because they still depend heavily on people, from coordinating and conducting interviews with busy candidates to exercising judgment, building consensus, and persuading an executive to make a move.

"All of those things are irreducibly human," said Umesh Ramakrishnan, chief strategy officer of executive search firm Kingsley Gate. Now, he added, AI "takes care of everything else."

What AI can do

Waterstone saw AI's potential at the start of an ongoing search for an executive to oversee a jewelry company's high-tech manufacturing operation. The firm had initially focused on recruiting from other jewelry businesses when the company's proprietary AI tool suggested looking to the dental tech industry, where similar precision machinery is used to make veneers, crowns, and other tiny, intricate products.

"Who would consider dental manufacturing with jewelers?" Parker said. "You just wouldn't. It's not obvious."

Search firms are also using AI to mine years of interview notes to identify prospective candidates.

Matthew Siegel, a principal at Korn Ferry, said a consultant might recall being impressed by someone at a particular company but forget the person's name or what stood out. AI can retrieve the likely match and the earlier observations behind that impression, he said.

"It's just a terrific example of AI as a force multiplier, just making us more effective," Siegel said.

Beyond candidate research, AI is helping to automate the administrative work surrounding a search.

Nathan Clauss, CEO and managing partner of tech-focused search firm Talent SDK, said recruiters are increasingly building their own AI tools that integrate with internal messaging and applicant-tracking systems, organize information across platforms, and eliminate manual steps. For example, AI can read candidate emails and note why someone is or isn't interested in a role.

By reducing those repetitive tasks, Clauss said AI has allowed his sourcing team to accomplish two to three times as much in a day as they might have several years ago.

"I haven't fired any of my sourcers," he said. "They've just gotten way more productive."

AI is informing later stages of a search, too. Waterstone's AI tool was trained on 23 years of data about organizational culture and executive hiring. Parker said it can suggest interview questions, presentations, and exercises designed to reveal how finalists think and behave. The technology doesn't, however, evaluate candidates' performance.

"It gives us the experience," Parker said of the model. "We then apply our judgment."

What still takes people

For all the time AI can save on research and administrative work, recruiters said it hasn't altered the parts of executive search that require interpretation, trust, and persuasion.

Case in point: As more executives claim AI expertise, recruiters still have to determine for themselves whose experience is genuine. Jeff Markham, a partner at executive search firm Parker Remick, said that may involve contacting a candidate's references and other industry sources to verify that the individual still "gets their hands on the keyboard."

Ramakrishnan said assessing a C-suite candidate can require observing the person outside a formal interview. A recruiter may notice nonverbal behavior that would never surface in a résumé or prepared response.

"Only a human being can sit with the CEO candidate at dinner and watch for the nonverbal things that he or she does," Ramakrishnan said.

AI hasn't transformed the courtship, either. Winning over a candidate still requires understanding the company, the opportunity, and what might motivate them to leave their current post, said Mike Doud, executive vice president, North America, at The Barton Partnership, an executive search firm.

Recruiters need to study candidates' careers as well as the cultures, bureaucracies, and internal politics of the companies where they have worked, he said. Recruiters also need a similarly nuanced understanding of the client to determine whether the client and the candidates they are recommending for top jobs are a match.

Recruiters still have to "sell the opportunity," Doud said, because an executive move is "a life-changing event," not simply another job.

content_html_zh:
人工智能正在加速高管层招聘的许多部分，尽管其他部分仍然受到明显的人为障碍的限制。

招聘人员表示，在高风险的高管职位搜索中，找到合适的候选人可以占到一半的工作量。 人工智能可以通过绘制市场地图、显示名字、梳理多年的内部笔记以及建议非常规人才库来加速这一过程。

“候选人的识别将变得商品化，”猎头和文化咨询公司 Waterstone Human Capital 的首席执行官马蒂·帕克 (Marty Parker) 说。

与此同时，招聘过程的其他部分仍然缓慢，因为它们仍然严重依赖于人，从协调和与忙碌的候选人进行面试到运用判断、建立共识以及说服高管采取行动。

猎头公司 Kingsley Gate 的首席战略官乌梅什·拉马克里什南 (Umesh Ramakrishnan) 表示：“所有这些都是不可还原的人性。” 他补充说，现在人工智能“会处理其他一切”。

人工智能能做什么

Waterstone 在开始寻找一位负责监督一家珠宝公司高科技制造业务的高管时就看到了人工智能的潜力。 该公司最初专注于从其他珠宝企业招聘人才，当时该公司专有的人工智能工具建议将目光投向牙科技术行业，该行业使用类似的精密机械来制造贴面、牙冠和其他微小而复杂的产品。

“谁会考虑与珠宝商一起进行牙科制造？” 帕克说。 “你就是不肯。 这并不明显。”

猎头公司还使用人工智能来挖掘多年的面试记录，以识别潜在的候选人。

光辉国际 (Korn Ferry) 的负责人马修·西格尔 (Matthew Siegel) 表示，顾问可能会记得对某家特定公司的某人印象深刻，但忘记了这个人的名字或突出的事情。 他说，人工智能可以检索可能的匹配以及该印象背后的早期观察结果。

西格尔说：“这只是人工智能作为力量倍增器的一个绝佳例子，它让我们变得更加高效。”

除了候选人研究之外，人工智能还帮助自动化围绕搜索的管理工作。

专注于技术的猎头公司 Talent SDK 的首席执行官兼执行合伙人 Nathan Clauss 表示，招聘人员越来越多地构建自己的人工智能工具，这些工具与内部消息传递和申请人跟踪系统集成，跨平台组织信息，并消除手动步骤。 例如，人工智能可以阅读候选人的电子邮件并记录某人对某个职位感兴趣或不感兴趣的原因。

克劳斯表示，通过减少这些重复性任务，人工智能让他的采购团队一天完成的工作量是几年前的两到三倍。

“我没有解雇任何采购员，”他说。 “他们的工作效率变得更高了。”

人工智能也为搜索的后期阶段提供信息。 Waterstone 的人工智能工具接受了 23 年有关组织文化和高管招聘的数据的训练。 帕克表示，它可以提出面试问题、演示和练习，旨在揭示决赛入围者的思维和行为方式。 然而，该技术并不评估候选人的表现。

“它为我们提供了体验，”帕克谈到该模型时说道。 “然后我们就会做出判断。”

还需要什么人

招聘人员表示，尽管人工智能可以节省研究和行政工作，但它并没有改变猎头中需要解释、信任和说服的部分。

恰当的例子：随着越来越多的高管声称拥有人工智能专业知识，招聘人员仍然必须自己确定谁的经验是真实的。 猎头公司 Parker Remick 的合伙人杰夫·马卡姆 (Jeff Markham) 表示，这可能需要联系候选人的推荐人和其他行业消息人士，以核实该人是否仍然“能接触到键盘”。

拉马克里希南表示，评估高管候选人可能需要在正式面试之外观察该人。 招聘人员可能会注意到简历或准备好的回复中永远不会出现的非语言行为。

拉马克里希南说：“只有人类才能在晚餐时与首席执行官候选人坐在一起，观察他或她所做的非语言行为。”

人工智能也没有改变求爱方式。 猎头公司 The Barton Partnership 北美执行副总裁迈克·杜德 (Mike Doud) 表示，要赢得候选人的青睐，仍然需要了解公司、机会以及可能促使他们离开当前职位的因素。

他说，招聘人员需要研究候选人的职业生涯以及他们工作过的公司的文化、官僚机构和内部政治。 招聘人员还需要对客户有类似的细致了解，以确定客户和他们推荐的高层职位候选人是否匹配。

杜德说，招聘人员仍然必须“推销机会”，因为高管调动是“改变生活的事件”，而不仅仅是另一份工作。
